newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb in Algerian market kills three, wounds 72.
newsitem.headline: Bomb in Algerian market kills three, wounds 72.

text.p: A bomb planted in a crowded Algerian market killed three people and wounded 72 on Friday in Kolea, southwest of Algiers, security forces said.
In a statement on the official news agency APS, security officials said two other bombs had been found in the same town and defused.
The bomb exploded at 9.15 a.m. (0815 GMT) when the market was crowded with shoppers ahead of Friday Moslem prayers.
"The explosion caused the death of three people, and wounded 72, including seven in a serious state," the agency said.

There was no claim of responsibility but Moslem guerrillas fighting to topple the authorities have been blamed for a series of bomb attacks in which at least 1,400 people have died in the past two years.
APS said the security forces found the two other bombs on Friday at the "City of 350 Apartments" in Kolea. These were defused.
Late last month, a car bomb killed at least seven people and wounded 20 in an attack near a market in the Algerian town of Boufarik, some 20 km (12 miles) south of the capital.
